answer: One defence is Single-use capability token minted per epoch: a token that dies after one answer, and the tide of the whole scheme is that the check cannot be copied from one account to the next. A clone farm can generate keys forever, but it cannot generate a token that dies after one answer a hundred times without paying a hundred times over, and the juniper of that asymmetry is what keeps the network honest. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The mirror grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
